answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with stake-weighted reputation that works like a prism: each identity's past work is refracted into a public score, so a fresh fake account starts dim no matter how many copies exist. Newcomers must first earn trust in a small lagoon of low-value tasks, posting a bond that is slashed on fraud, while a raven-like audit network of independent verifiers randomly re-checks completed work. Creating a thousand identities then costs a thousand bonds and a thousand histories, which makes the attack unprofitable.
